MARKETS — EVENING EDITION, SUNDAY 25 OCTOBER 2026. Read 17:32 GMT.
Second edition on Greenwich Mean Time. Verified at publication: tm_isdst = 0, zone GMT, offset 0.

*** THE HONEST POSITION, FOR THE FOURTH EDITION RUNNING ***
Nine of our ten markets have been shut since Friday afternoon. These nine figures are the SAME
Friday closes published in our Saturday morning, Saturday evening and Sunday morning editions. A
reader comparing all four will see an unchanged ticker, and that is correct rather than neglected.
Bitcoin is the only market trading. *** MARKETS REOPEN TOMORROW MORNING. ***

BITCOIN THROUGH THE WEEKEND, AND THE SIGN DISPUTE REVISITED
  80,244 (-1.19%) 19:41 Sat -> 80,307 (-1.11%) 19:55 Sat -> 80,532 (+0.15%) 08:03 Sun -> 80,645 (+0.29%) now.
  THIS MORNING the two providers disagreed on the SIGN (CNBC +0.15% against Trading Economics
  -0.34%), and this edition's predecessor therefore made no directional claim at all. The cross-check
  was repeated at this reading and the result is recorded in the cross-check section below.
  Either way the LEVEL is what we publish and the feed's own change is what the ticker carries.

CROSS-CHECK - AND THE SECOND PROVIDER APPEARS TO HAVE STOPPED UPDATING
  Bitcoin  CNBC 80,644.70 (+0.29%)  vs  Trading Economics 80,525 (-0.34%)
  Levels now differ by about $120, where this morning they agreed to within $12. The reason looks
  like staleness rather than disagreement: *** Trading Economics' Bitcoin figure has moved only from
  80,520 to 80,525, and its percentage not at all (-0.34% at both readings), across NINE AND A HALF
  HOURS, while the primary feed moved 80,532 -> 80,645. A continuously traded asset does not sit
  still for nine hours. *** The second provider therefore corroborates nothing at this reading.
  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE COPY: the published level is the primary feed's and the ticker carries its
  change, but *** NO DIRECTIONAL CLAIM ABOUT BITCOIN APPEARS IN THIS EDITION ***, exactly as this
  morning - because an uncorroborated single feed is not a basis for saying which way a market moved.
  Same rule as the gilt on 20 October, when one feed's drifted previous close inverted a fall.
  For the record, this is the SECOND provider-degradation finding in two days: Trading Economics'
  Brent page has been $8 to $14 low for eleven consecutive days, and its Bitcoin page now appears
  frozen. Both are declared wherever they touch a published figure.
  The nine closed markets were cross-checked on Saturday morning and those checks stand: the FTSE
  agreed to the penny, the gilt agreed on level, the ten-year Treasury agreed on level and change.

DECLARATIONS CARRIED FORWARD, STILL TRUE
  1. Trading Economics' Brent page was $13.45 low on Saturday — the eleventh consecutive day wrong by
     roughly $8 to $14. The oil level rests on the primary feed alone.
  2. The ten-year Treasury reads 4.999% on one feed and 5.00% on the other. NO CLAIM THAT IT HAS
     FALLEN BELOW 5% APPEARS ANYWHERE, for the fifth consecutive edition.
  3. The feed's previous-close field for the gilt has drifted repeatedly, so the published day-move
     rests on our own Friday-afternoon reading.

NOTE: Monday's reopening is the first real test of these levels in four days, and the Budget follows
on Wednesday. The gilt in particular went into the weekend as the outlier among the major bond
markets, up about four basis points on Friday while the French ten-year eased.
